item.title: 59th Annual Lunsford Festival — Sat Oct 3, 10:00 AM — Mars Hill University
item.description:
The event is the second longest-running folk festival in Western North Carolina and was named in honor of Bascom Lamar Lunsford, who was a musician and folklorist who dedicated his life to collecting and promoting the music of Southern Appalachia. Please join us in honoring the rich cultural traditions of the Southern Appalachian Mountains! In addition to mountain music and dance all day on the upper quad, the festival will also feature an open jam guided by master musicians, a roundtable discussion about banjo-player Carroll Best, a ballad swap, and a Lunsford sing-a-long. Bring a blanket and your favorite camp chair, and be sure to leave your car behind – there will be shuttles running from the Ingles on 213 to campus (see bottom of this page for info).
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Bent Creek-Sidehill: 7 mi 1000 ft elev. gain — Fri Oct 9, 9:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **[Sign-up opens Sunday, Oct. 4th, 8:00 pm]**
This is a "Todd Hike" that's mostly on Lower Sidehill Trail and South Ridge Rd. It's a pretty area deep into Bent Creek. The plan is for a "lollipop" with a short stem at the start and finish, and a big loop the rest of the way.
Be prepared for a moderate pace, around 2.4 mph. There's good footing throughout, with a combination of forest trails and gravel roads. Ups and downs are relatively mild. If you're on the fence about poles, you probably won't need them here. Bring water and, if you're inclined, a snack, too. There'll be a little break somewhere around the middle.
**CARPOOLING TIME & PLACE**
There's limited trailhead parking, so we'll carpool from the Asheville Outlets behind the Waffle House (directions below). Look for me and my silver Hyundai. Come early to allow for traffic. We'll depart by 9:00 AM

AVL Digital Nomads Confession time: we love our people. Maybe a little too much. At every social, we see the same happy circles, and we get it. Your friends are great. But somewhere out there tonight is your next great friend, and you haven't met them yet.
So here's the challenge.
**The Rules**
1. From 6:00 to 7:30, you can't talk to anyone you knew before tonight. 2. Waves are free. Conversations are not. 3. Came with a friend? Split up at 6:00 sharp.
**The Stakes:** If you're caught chatting with someone you already know, you both owe a beverage (booze optional) to whoever called you out. Yes, your friends will absolutely be watching you.
**The Reunion:** At 7:30, find your crew and bring at least one new friend with you.

item.title: Jackson Grimm's Old Time Machine — Sat Nov 21, 8:30 PM
item.description:
Jackson Grimm marries folk pop melodies with the lonesome sound of traditional Appalachian music. In a region with a strong music culture, it is no surprise that Grimm's songwriting is representative of his musical birthplace: Asheville, NC.
His Appalachian-infused Americana songs run the gamut from a traditional country waltz homage ("If Not For You") to an unrequited love song driven by a Beatles-esque melody ("I'd Hold You, But I Don't Wanna Hold You)" to a drunken Old Crow Medicine Show-style partygrass number ("Last Train Home").
Grimm studied Traditonal Music at Warren Wilson College under the tutelage of renowned players like Wayne Erbsen and Kevin Kehrberg. He also studied guitar, banjo, mandolin & singing with the Western North Carolina music master, Josh Goforth.
